My land here in Quzhou has always been wheat and corn. My father grew wheat and corn, I grew wheat and corn, and I will grow wheat and corn again this year. The winters are cold, the summers are hot, and that's what fits the land and the seasons here. I have 8 mu. I plant wheat in October when the soil cools and the rains have come, then after the June harvest I turn the ground and put in corn right away before the summer heat peaks. I have done this for fifty years.

For seeds, I go to the village supply station and buy whatever improved variety they have. The hybrid corn and the improved wheat give more grain than the old seeds my grandfather kept. I don't know the science of it, but I know the yields.

For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer at planting and then top-dress with urea later. My son says I put on too much, but I have seen lean years when I applied less, and I don't want to risk it. Better to have a little extra in the ground.

For wheat I water four times — once in winter to protect the roots from freezing, again at jointing, at heading, and at grain filling. For corn I water once at planting if it is dry, and once more if August is bad. We have always relied on the summer rains for corn.

I spray herbicide on the wheat in autumn and again in spring, then a fungicide spray before heading because rust and powdery mildew come every few years. For corn, one herbicide pass and one pesticide spray if I see pests.

Before wheat I rotary till the field. After wheat harvest, I plant the corn with minimal tillage — the ground is already worked from the wheat season and I want to get the corn in fast.
